preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 200 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 200 and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 200 and int(line.split()[0]) != int(line.split()[1]) and 0 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 1 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200) and m (n-1 ≤ m ≤ 2000). Each of the next m lines contains three integers i, j, b (1 ≤ i, j ≤ n, i ≠ j, 0 ≤ b ≤ 1), representing a friendship between i and j with envy direction b (1 means i is envious of j, 0 means undirected).
The input consists of exactly m + 1 lines (first line for n and m, followed by m friendship lines).
Each friendship line contains exactly three integers.

postconditions.description: If there exists a valid income assignment satisfying all envy constraints, output 'YES' followed by the maximum possible income inequality and the corresponding incomes. Otherwise, output 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'NO') or (all(0 <= int(a) <= 10**6 for a in stdout.splitlines()[2].split()) and len(stdout.splitlines()[2].split()) == n)
postconditions.description: If 'YES', the second line is the maximum possible income inequality (max(a_i) - min(a_i)), and the third line contains n integers representing valid incomes a_1, ..., a_n (0 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^6).

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip() == 'YES') == (all(1 <= i <= n and 1 <= j <= n and i != j for i, j, b in parse_friendships(stdin)) and all(0 <= b <= 1 for i, j, b in parse_friendships(stdin)))
postconditions.description: The output 'YES' or 'NO' is determined solely by the feasibility of assigning incomes such that for every friendship (i,j) with b=1, a_j = a_i + 1, and for every friendship (i,j) with b=0, either a_i = a_j + 1 or a_j = a_i + 1.
If 'YES', the maximum income inequality (max(a_i) - min(a_i)) is correctly computed and printed as the second line.
